dashboard.deliveryRiskCompareSimpleNote: Node pass counts only observed delivery to a different node or terminal server; same-node retries are excluded. With a configured terminal mail server, a settled chain with no next hop is counted as a node block; without a terminal target it remains unconfirmed. Different decision = node block with Vigilyx safe + node pass with Vigilyx risky.
dashboard.deliveryRiskCompareNote: Node actions come from passive SMTP path evidence, not a vendor threat-verdict API. An observed next hop is a pass; SMTP 550–554 with 5.7.x after a completed message transaction is an explicit rejection; with a configured terminal target, no next hop after settlement is path-termination blocking. The two evidence types remain distinct in details; without a terminal target, missing next hops remain unconfirmed. A message can appear at multiple nodes, so node counts must not be added together.

dataSecurity.classificationBoundary: JR/T 0197-2020 uses levels 1–5. JR/T 0171-2020 personal financial categories C1–C3 are separate. These detection candidates require the institution’s approved catalog and impact assessment.
dataSecurity.candidateLevel5: Potentially exceptionally severe impact on multiple institutions or the financial system requires institutional assessment. No single field automatically establishes this level. State secrets are outside the guide’s scope.
dataSecurity.candidateLevel4: Authentication credentials, CVV and authentication biometrics. OTP combined with account information may escalate to this level.

dataSecurity.candidateLevel2: Internal business information candidates; adjust for content, purpose, combinations and impact.
dataSecurity.candidateLevel1: Public reference candidates. Public SWIFT/BIC and registration information alone do not trigger sensitive transfer incidents; linked customer data is assessed separately.
dataSecurity.bulkEscalationDesc: Rolling {{hours}} hours: {{high}} level-4 field matches create a Critical bulk incident; {{sensitive}} level-3+ matches create a High bulk incident, with a {{cooldown}}-minute cooldown. These are product thresholds, not legal allowances; single-item alerts remain active. Aggregation currently covers observed HTTP transfers and resets on process restart.
dataSecurity.policyScenarioDesc_submission: Ordinary recipients, self-sends and file transit are inspected. One sensitive field creates a risk incident. Submission does not establish successful delivery.
dataSecurity.policyScenarioDesc_draft: Sensitive drafts are recorded separately and excluded from bulk transfer totals. A draft does not establish leakage or delivery.
dataSecurity.policyScenarioDesc_publicReference: Public SWIFT/BIC alone does not alert as a sensitive transfer. Normal login requests are outside send detection. Other sensitive content is checked independently.
dataSecurity.authorizationPolicyNotice: A verified business authorization registry is not configured. An allowlisted domain does not establish authorization. Incidents remain unverified pending review of purpose, recipients, legal basis, approvals and channel.
dataSecurity.regulatoryRequirementsDesc: Apply business necessity, least privilege, assessment and approval before external provision, recipient verification, applicable consent or statutory basis, authentication data protection and audit logs. Apply PBOC and banking/insurance rules according to institutional and business scope.
dataSecurity.bankInsuranceRules: Banking and Insurance Data Security Measures (2024 No. 24)
dataSecurity.observationBoundaryDesc: Mirror mode observes and alerts. MTA quarantine, rejection and relay outcomes are recorded separately. Transfer risk, actual delivery and legal conclusions require separate verification.

dataSecurity.incidentTypeDesc_bulk_sensitive_transfer: Observed transfers reached product bulk thresholds; these are not statutory limits.

emailSecurity.sceneDetectionScopeDesc: Each rule aggregates completed SMTP sessions over a time window instead of scoring one email in isolation. A match creates a scene record; automatic blocking still depends on the scene's configuration and thresholds.
emailSecurity.bulkMailingLogic: In the last {{hours}} hours, completed SMTP emails are grouped by external sender domain; the scene triggers when emails ≥ {{emails}} and unique internal recipients ≥ {{recipients}}.
emailSecurity.bulkMailingEvidence: Evidence: sender domain, completed SMTP status, and the set of internal recipients; internal sender domains and configured exclusions are omitted.
emailSecurity.bounceHarvestLogic: Within {{hours}} hours, group raw NDRs by source and internal target domain; correlate and deduplicate appliance report records across messages. Create a scene at ≥ {{bounces}} failures and ≥ {{targets}} targets. Sparse report correlation is separately enabled.
emailSecurity.bounceHarvestEvidence: Evidence: structured NDR or report records. Deduplicate NDRs by session and failed target, reports by original message identity, claimed sender and failed target. Report identities are unverified; observations do not alter this message verdict.
emailSecurity.internalDomainImpersonationLogic: In the last {{hours}} hours, only external sender domains are checked; the scene triggers when a similar internal domain is found and emails ≥ {{emails}}. Similarity includes TLD swaps, spelling changes, homoglyphs, and boundary-aware prefixes/suffixes.
emailSecurity.internalDomainImpersonationEvidence: Evidence: Punycode is decoded before comparing domain bases; short domains are skipped, and the matching internal domain and impersonation type are stored in the scene details.

pipeline.thresholdsHint: V2 uses malicious Bel, named attack constraints and independent-cause guards. Identity review sets a 40% Medium floor for a random sender domain or From/Reply-To domain mismatch.
pipeline.alertFloorFactorHint: Scales the risk floor from an eligible source score in the default strategy; must be ≥ 1.0 (range 1.00 – 3.00). The legacy strategy applies it to module belief.
pipeline.convergenceBaseFloorHint: Base risk floor for qualified convergence across independent causal keys and evidence clusters; a contextual-only rule may cap the result. Minimum 0.40 (range 0.40 – 0.85).
pipeline.convergenceBeliefThresholdHint: Despite the historical field name, this compares normalized source score. Convergence also requires independent causal keys, distinct evidence clusters, and an eligible native source (range (0, 0.10]).
pipeline.alertBeliefThresholdHint: Historical configuration compatibility field; current D-S V2 does not read this value.
pipeline.epsilonHint: Open-world uncertainty mass of DS fusion; maps to the backend default_epsilon field (range (0, 0.50])
pipeline.saveThresholdsHint: The engine reloads the config after saving; applies to subsequent mail verdicts
